sam: Quick question — where should the "policy translator" live for hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private)? I'm leaning toward a small control-plane translator that emits compact runtime directives, but want to surface tradeoffs before an RFC.
rita: agree with exploring control-plane first. biggest concern is private installs without control-plane access — latency and upgrade cadence differ a lot.
matt: another big one is secrets/KMS bindings. if control-plane translates and signs directives, private deployments need a trust flow to accept them. can't just hand over raw credentials.
sam: yeah. thought: control-plane = default translator that outputs a signed, minimal directive bundle (checksum + version). runtime validates signature and applies. private installs can opt-in to pulling translator artifacts or run a local translator.
alex: fallback semantics matter. if runtime can't reach control-plane for translation, do we: 1) fail fast, 2) accept last-known directive, or 3) run in permissive mode? each has safety/cost implications. My vote = last-known directive with an explicit TTL.
sara: for private/on-prem we should allow a packaged translator binary as an escape hatch. ops teams can run it locally and we keep the interface identical (same directive schema). reduces secret surface since translation happens where KMS lives.
matt: +1 to packaged translator for private. for hosted/dedicated we can centralize translation but need a key-rotation plan: signed bundles, short-lived signing keys, and a verification endpoint. I'll sketch a draft keyflow.
infra-bot: deploy: policy-translator-staging v0.1 deployed to staging cluster (sha: a1b2c3).
sam: sketch of directive schema (very small):
```json
{"version":"v1","directive_id":"uuid","ops":[{"route":"/generate","quota":"1000/min","batching":"auto"}],"issued_at":"ts","ttl_secs":3600,"sig":"..."}
```
rita: that looks reasonable. need an explicit field for "source_mode" indicating where translator ran (control-plane|local) so audits can trace policy origin.
alex: agree. also include a "grace_window_secs" for last-known directives so runtime knows when to force failover policies.
sam: proposed hybrid pattern summary: control-plane translator by default, signed minimal bundles; packaged/local translator for private; runtime supports last-known TTL + grace window; clear audit field for origin.
sara: sounds good. can we capture these tradeoffs in a short RFC + a test matrix (latency, verification overhead, failure scenarios)?
sam: yep — action items: I will open RFC with this hybrid proposal + sample schema today. @matt please add key rotation sketch and KMS constraints; @rita add testing matrix for private installs. infra-bot: issue created: ARCH-1482 (policy-translator-rfc).
matt: will do.
sara: will help validate packaged translator UX with a quick install script.
sam: thanks — we'll review RFC next Tue. :thumbsup:
